questions.question: How old was Ramesses II when he ascended to the throne?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Ramesses ascended to the throne at age 25.
Incorrect. Eleven was Ramesses II's approximate age when his grandfather Ramesses I was appointed successor by Horemheb, not when Ramesses II himself ascended.
Incorrect. Fourteen was the approximate age at which Ramesses II was designated prince regent by his father Seti I, not when he became pharaoh.
Incorrect. Ninety or ninety-one is the estimated age at Ramesses II's death, not his age at accession.

questions.question: How many military campaigns did Ramesses II conduct?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Ramesses II conducted no fewer than 15 military campaigns, all resulting in victories except the Battle of Kadesh.
Incorrect. Thirteen or fourteen refers to the number of Sed festivals Ramesses celebrated, not his military campaigns.
Incorrect. Sixty-six is the length of Ramesses II's reign in years, not the number of campaigns.
Incorrect. Twenty-one is the regnal year in which Ramesses concluded the peace treaty with the Hittites, not the number of campaigns.

questions.question: What name was Ramesses II called in ancient Greek sources?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in ancient Greek sources, he is called Ozymandias.
Incorrect. Usermaatre Setepenre is part of his Egyptian-language regnal name, from which Ozymandias is derived, not the Greek name itself.
Incorrect. Riamessesa is the pronunciation of Ramesses indicated by cuneiform letters, not the ancient Greek name.
Incorrect. Wasmuriya Satepnaria Riamessesa Maiamana is the full titulary pronunciation from cuneiform letters, not the ancient Greek name.

questions.question: Where is Ramesses II's mummy currently on display?
options: National Museum of Egyptian Civilization in Cairo
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states his mummy is now on display at the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization, located in Cairo.
Incorrect. KV7 in the Valley of the Kings was his original burial place, not where his mummy is displayed today.
Incorrect. The Royal Cache was where his body was later moved and discovered in 1881, not its current display location.
Incorrect. Pi-Ramesses was the city he established as Egypt's new capital, not a museum location.

questions.question: How many Sed festivals did Ramesses II celebrate?

Incorrect. Fifteen refers to the number of military campaigns Ramesses conducted, not Sed festivals.
Incorrect. Sixty-six is the length of his reign in years, not the number of Sed festivals.
Incorrect. Twenty-one is the year he concluded the peace treaty with the Hittites, not the number of Sed festivals.

questions.question: Which city did Ramesses II establish as Egypt's new capital?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that after establishing Pi-Ramesses in the Nile Delta, he designated it as Egypt's new capital.
Incorrect. Thebes is not mentioned in the article as Ramesses II's new capital.
Incorrect. Memphis is not mentioned in the article as Ramesses II's new capital.
Incorrect. Heliopolis is mentioned as a place where Ramesses was back in Egypt by November 1272 BC, not as his new capital.

questions.question: How long was Ramesses II's reign?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states his 66-year rule was the longest recorded reign of any pharaoh.
Incorrect. Over 90 years is the reign attributed to Pepi II, not Ramesses II.
Incorrect. Twenty-five is Ramesses II's age when he ascended the throne, not his reign length.
Incorrect. Twenty-one is the regnal year in which he concluded the peace treaty with the Hittites, not his reign length.

questions.question: In which year of his reign did Ramesses II conclude the peace treaty with the Hittites?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in Year 21 of Ramesses's reign (1259 BC), he concluded the peace treaty with the Hittites known as the Treaty of Kadesh.
Incorrect. Year 2 was when Ramesses II defeated the Sherden sea pirates, not when the peace treaty was concluded.
Incorrect. Year 4 was when his first Syrian campaign took place, not when the peace treaty was concluded.
Incorrect. Year 5 was when the Battle of Kadesh occurred, not when the peace treaty was concluded.

questions.question: What was Ramesses II's grandfather's name?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Ramesses II's grandfather was Ramesses I, a vizier and military officer during Horemheb's reign.
Incorrect. Seti I was Ramesses II's father, not his grandfather.
Incorrect. Horemheb was the pharaoh who appointed Ramesses I as his successor; he was not Ramesses II's grandfather.
Incorrect. Merneptah was Ramesses II's son, not his grandfather.
